target_columns.name: region
target_columns.transformation: Blank/missing region recoded to 'UNKNOWN' before grouping

target_columns.name: product_line
target_columns.transformation: Pass-through grouping key; set to literal 'ALL' on the inserted region subtotal row

target_columns.name: total_sum_insured
target_columns.transformation: Sum of sum_insured grouped by region+product_line; on subtotal row, replaced with running sum of total_sum_insured across all product lines in that region

target_columns.name: policy_count
target_columns.transformation: Count (N) of policies grouped by region+product_line; on subtotal row, replaced with running sum of policy_count across all product lines in that region

quirks: Blank region values are recoded to literal string 'UNKNOWN' before aggregation, not dropped or nulled -- must preserve exact string match

A synthetic subtotal row is injected per region after the last product_line (product_line='ALL'), mixing detail and aggregate rows in the same output table -- any downstream consumer or Spark equivalent must either replicate this row-injection or the migration must explicitly flag/separate it

The subtotal computation uses SAS BY-group RETAIN logic on pre-sorted data (by region, product_line) -- product_line sort order determines which row is 'last' in the region and therefore where the ALL row lands; must sort identically before computing subtotals in PySpark (e.g. window function with lag/lead or union of detail + groupBy(region) aggregate, re-sorted by region+product_line so 'ALL' sorts correctly after real product lines)

policy_count is a row count (N) via PROC MEANS, not a distinct policy ID count -- if source has duplicate/multiple rows per policy this would double count; must confirm one-row-per-policy assumption holds

No explicit handling for sum_insured being null/missing -- PROC MEANS sum= silently excludes missing values from sum but N still counts rows with class vars present, so policy_count could include policies with null sum_insured while total_sum_insured excludes their contribution

Final output is only sorted by region+product_line, not by any numeric subtotal flag, so 'ALL' relies on string sort order being greater than actual product_line values to appear last within each region -- if any product_line value sorts after 'ALL' alphabetically this ordering assumption breaks
